features.text: Patient is 62 years old and male.
Patient is here for an annual exam.
Patient has a history of depression.
Patient has a history of hypertension.
Patient had a lobectomy a few years back.
Patient has been managing depression with medication.
Patient has been struggling with hypertension, especially on weekends when he sometimes forgets to take his meds.
Patient runs 4 to 5 miles a day.
Patient experiences shortness of breath and a pounding in his chest during runs, especially in humid conditions.
The chest pounding feels like a slight, rhythmic thumping in the chest, almost like the heart is beating a little harder than usual.
The chest pounding usually goes away on its own after a few minutes.
The chest pounding episodes usually last a few minutes, up to five minutes.
The chest pounding episodes occur occasionally, especially on hot or humid days during runs.
The patient has not experienced any episodes of chest pain, dizziness, or syncope during or after the chest pounding episodes.
The patient has not experienced any episodes of palpitations, lightheadedness, or syncope in the past.
The patient has not had any recent changes in his medication regimen for hypertension or depression.
The patient has not started any new medications recently.
The patient has no specific information about his family history of cardiovascular disease.
The patient knows he has a history of hypertension but is unsure about his relatives' medical histories.
The patient has not noticed any changes in the frequency or intensity of the chest pounding episodes over the past few months.
